title: Local representative calculation before global target transport
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ and $h:X'\to X$ be arbitrary scheme morphisms, $q:U\to X$ etale, $F$ an etale sheaf of sets, and $t$ a global section of $i^*F$ in its identity-pullback presentation. Let $s\in F(U)$ satisfy that its unit image under $i$ is the restriction of $t$ along the base change of $q:U\to X$. Put $Z'=Z\times_X X'$, $j:Z'\to X'$ and $p:Z'\to Z$, and $k=h\circ j$. For one open $W\subset X'$ and $\phi:W\to U$ with $q\circ\phi=h\circ W.\iota$, use the local representative and preimage-open isomorphism of [def-weil-pbc-gabber-h0-zariski-constructions]. Apply the unit for $j$ to the local representative, restrict through the preimage-open isomorphism, and apply the component of the chosen composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] at $j^{-1}W$. The resulting section equals the section comparison of $t$ along $p$ from [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison], restricted first along the canonical top-open-to-identity-pullback isomorphism for $k$ and then to $j^{-1}W$. No global target section $t_H$, Zariski comparison $\beta$, covering or closed-immersion hypothesis is used. The scheme fibre product, etale sheaf and etale morphism notions are those of [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets, def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: Move the restriction defining the local representative through the unit for j by unit naturality, and through the chosen composition comparison by its naturality. Its unit equation gives the unit for k restricted along the preimage-open map, the base change of the representative map and inverse pasting.

The composition-unit equation along p and i identifies this unit with section comparison applied to the unit for i. Substitute the representative compatibility assumption. Restriction naturality of section comparison moves the base change of U to X outside this comparison.

The resulting map into the identity pullback equals the restriction-to-top followed by the canonical top-pullback isomorphism. Both are over Z-prime, and the second projection of the identity pullback is an isomorphism; cancel it. Presheaf functoriality gives the two successive restrictions. Empty opens obey the same formal computation.
